jobs._note_2026_09_17: bfs_weekly.csv had answered 404 on every run since 16 Sep; the weekly files live under three names (US, state, region), found and registered 17 Sep 2026. WBA_NSA is the weekly form of leg F's object (applications with planned wages), by state.

jobs.name: intl_keyless
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026 for the confidence programme (international and Canadian replication). Keyless doors, weekly refresh.

jobs.name: labour_attention
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Labour-demand, expectations and attention sources the rule does not yet read: weekly temp staffing, household expectations, news sentiment, reader attention. Raw files; series are derived downstream.

jobs.name: housing_hf
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Faster housing reads than monthly starts: weekly listings and inventory, monthly national tracker.

jobs.name: markets_daily
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Never-revised daily prices for sector proxies of the mechanisms the legs watch: copper, crude, small caps, transports, regional banks, homebuilders, credit ETFs, semis, retail, staffing and trucking shares. Yahoo chart API, full history.

jobs.name: central_banks_intl
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Balance-sheet family abroad (the family that passes the null at home) and zero-lag surveys, for the international runs.

jobs.name: intl_labour_live
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Live labour registers and rates abroad, plain fetches, a dated copy kept at each change: UK (ONS time-series generator: unemployment rate MGSX, claimant count BCJD, vacancies AP2Y), Ireland (CSO PxStat LRM02, Live Register monthly from 1967), Australia (ABS LF unemployment rate). The histories are already held in collections 19, 46 and 58; this keeps them current and builds their vintages. France (DARES open data, keyless): registered jobseekers' entries and exits by departement monthly from 1996 (the regional inflow panel the international work named as its next acquisition), the stock, and job offers collected by departement (a vacancy object). UK claimant count by region (from January 1986) and by 406 local authorities (Nomis NM_162_1, keyless).

jobs.name: release_pdfs
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The current-release documents of the series the live rule reads, at their standing addresses; each is overwritten by its publisher at the next release, so a dated copy is kept every time one changes. From today the first print of every rule object is on disk as it was published: the weekly claims release (claims, insured unemployment, the state table), the Employment Situation, JOLTS, state employment, new residential construction, G.17, the commercial paper release.

jobs.name: fed_ddp
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The Board's Data Download Program: each statistical release whole, as a zip, at a standing address. A dated copy at each change is a complete vintage of the release: G.17 production and capacity, H.8 bank assets and liabilities, G.19 consumer credit, H.15 rates, commercial paper, H.4.1, Z.1, G.20, charge-offs and delinquencies, household debt service, H.6, H.3, policy rates.

jobs.name: bea_flat
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Every NIPA table in one file (20 MB); a dated copy at each change is a complete vintage of the national accounts, personal income and outlays included.

jobs.name: philadelphia_rtdsm
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The Philadelphia Fed's Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists, the five workbooks that answered: unemployment rate, payroll employment, hours, housing starts, labour force (monthly vintages from 1965). Collection 21 holds a copy taken earlier; this keeps it current.

jobs.name: bls_flat_files
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The Bureau of Labor Statistics' whole databases as flat files: JOLTS, the household survey, the payroll survey, state and metropolitan payrolls, state unemployment. With a dated copy at each change this is a complete monthly vintage of everything the Bureau publishes, far beyond the 2,603 series on the ALFRED list. The host answers 403 to a bare browser string and 200 to the collector's declared one (tested natively 17 Sep 2026).

jobs.name: surveys_comparators
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026 (third pass). Real-time-by-construction surveys, published recession gauges to compare the rule against (never inputs), plumbing and freight.

jobs.name: dynamic_links
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Files whose address carries a date; each dated file is kept, so they accumulate as vintages.

jobs.name: feeds
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Release feeds of agencies, central banks and trade bodies: every item indexed once, its page or PDF fetched once and kept. A first-print archive that builds itself.

jobs.name: chicagofed
jobs.note: Chicago Fed data products through their keyless JSON manifests (data.chicagofed.org/cfed-drm-chicago/<product>): labor market indicators with the real-time unemployment forecast, CARTS weekly retail, CFNAI with its real-time workbooks, NFCI with its revisions table, survey of economic conditions. A dated copy is kept whenever a file changes. Added 17 Sep 2026.

jobs.name: kalshi
jobs.note: Kalshi: daily candles of the NBER recession contracts and their neighbours (next recession start, unemployment spike, negative GDP growth, Canada, world). Public market data, no key. Comparator only. Added 17 Sep 2026.

jobs.name: polymarket
jobs.note: Polymarket: daily price of every recession contract, open or closed (US 2024, 2025, by end of 2026, by end of 2027; Canada, UK, Japan). Public market data, no key. Comparator only. Added 17 Sep 2026.

jobs.name: socrata_sweep
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Discovery without AI: the public Socrata catalog searches every state, county and city portal; datasets whose name passes the relevance pattern are catalogued, then downloaded within a budget and fetched again when the source changes them.

jobs.name: sec_items
jobs.note: SEC EDGAR full-text search: 8-K filings by item, by filing date (public same day, never revised). 2.05 exit or disposal costs (layoffs, plant closings); 2.06 material impairments; 1.03 bankruptcy or receivership; 2.04 triggered acceleration of a debt; 3.01 notice of delisting. Added 17 Sep 2026.

jobs.name: sec_phrases
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Weekly counts of 8-K filings containing each phrase, EDGAR full-text search, 2001 on; weeks end on Saturday. Real time by construction (filing dates are never revised).

jobs.name: global_bulk
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. One-file doors to the world, keyless: ILO short-term indicators (monthly unemployment rate, unemployment and employment for about a hundred countries), the World Bank Global Economic Monitor (monthly activity, trade, prices), BIS bulk files (credit gaps, total credit, debt service ratios, property prices, policy rates). For the international tools; a dated copy at each change.

jobs.name: ecb_rtd
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The ECB real-time database (dataflow RTD): every value as published, with its publication timestamp, from January 2001 - euro-area unemployment, industrial production, new car registrations, money and trade, plus the unemployment rate of the United States and Japan.

jobs.name: bundesbank_realtime
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The Bundesbank real-time database (dataflow BBKRT), keyless: every release of German production, orders, employment and GDP since June 1995, each series key carrying its release date. A second international real-time vintage source beside the OECD revisions database. Large files, so fresh for 25 days. The service answers 413 while it prepares a large extract; the file then comes on a later cycle.

jobs.name: imf_sdmx
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The IMF's SDMX service (api.imf.org), keyless. Labor Statistics (employment, unemployed persons, unemployment rate, labour force, wage rates; 194 countries) and Production Indexes (118 countries), monthly from 1950 and quarterly, whole datasets in one request each (195 MB and 395 MB raw, 3 MB and 7 MB compressed: every row carries the dataset's description). A dated copy at each change builds the vintages the IMF does not serve: its own vintage dataflows (LS_2026_MAY_VINTAGE and the like) exist but return no observations without a login.

jobs.name: blind_spots
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Channels for the mechanisms the rule has no object for (register item 35). Checked first against what is already held: the grid is already covered (job eia carries EIA-930 hourly demand from the balance files and daily demand by region), and the demographic series are already in the FRED bulk pull, so neither is added again. What was genuinely missing: climate, and the fiscal accounts beyond the daily cash statement.

files._why: climate: every United States weather and climate disaster costing a billion dollars or more, 1980 on, with its dates and cost
climate: the share of the country at each drought severity, weekly from 2000
fiscal: the public debt every business day
fiscal: the Monthly Treasury Statement's receipts and outlays by source, which the daily cash statement does not classify
fiscal: withheld income and employment taxes as deposited each day, the fastest read on payrolls that exists

jobs.name: oecd_revisions
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. OECD short-term statistics revisions database: monthly editions (vintages) from Feb 1999; unemployment rate (UNEMP) and production volume (PRVM) per country. The API is rate-limited, so a cycle may fetch only part; files stay fresh 25 days and the rest follow on later cycles.

jobs.name: nimble
search_queries: public daily or weekly United States economic activity dataset csv download (restaurant, travel, freight, retail, hiring, consumer spending) real-time indicator

jobs.name: audit
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The quality gate: recomputes first, last, count and repeated share for every series and flags what has stalled, frozen, emptied or turned into a web page. Runs on the slow lane.

jobs.name: private_indicators
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The indicators the gap register called licensed or unavailable. Every one of them answered on the first try through the fetch engine (several only through its curl rung, which is why a plain urllib call had made them look shut). The page itself is kept, and a dated copy at every change: from today each month's first print of these numbers is held with the date it was published, which is what the rule's real-time standard needs and what a subscription would not give. The histories before today are a separate one-time harvest from the Internet Archive (ISM alone has 15,170 archived captures of its report pages, NFIB 417 of its monthly PDFs).

jobs.name: realtime_activity
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Weekly and daily measures of activity that are published once and never revised, which is the property the rule values most: rail carloads, raw steel production, mortgage applications, seated diners, small-business hours worked, bankruptcy filings, and the Spanish and New York Fed live series. Each was refused by a plain request before the fetch engine and answers now.

jobs.name: dated_files
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. Sources that publish at an address carrying the month or the week and give no readable index page. Every file is dated by construction, so the folder is a vintage archive in itself. The NFIB monthly report is the case that forced this: nfib.com answers 403 to every page and to its own search interface, while the report sits open at /wp-content/uploads/<year>/<month>/SBET-<Mon>-<year>.pdf.

jobs.name: state_deep
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026 in answer to 'collect all the state data we can'. Three state sources the warehouse did not hold: the Census building-permit files by state (one file a month since 1990, 972 of them on the server, the monthly first print of leg F's object at state level); the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages by state, which counts every covered job rather than sampling; and nothing here is revised once published except by the source's own schedule, so each dated file is a vintage by construction.

jobs.name: intl_comparables
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026. The countries whose labour data can be read the way the American state panel is read, at the unit below the country and at a real-time frequency: Mexico's social-security register (every insured job, by state, by month, never revised, the closest foreign analogue to covered employment); Germany's federal employment agency monthly report (registered unemployed by Land); Spain's registered unemployment and social-security affiliation by province; Canada's employment-insurance beneficiaries and labour force survey by province; Japan's and Korea's national series for the same months. The rule's international runs already hold the United Kingdom, Ireland, France and Australia.

jobs.name: state_files
jobs._note: Added 17 Sep 2026 in answer to 'collect all the state data we can'. The Labor Department's employment-security reports the warehouse did not hold (227 nonmonetary determinations, 218 benefit rights, 581 tax rates, 9050 first-payment timeliness, 207 the characteristics of the insured), the Bureau of Economic Analysis's regional archives whole (annual and quarterly state income and product), the housing finance agency's state price index, the Census quarterly tax series and the state electricity series. Each with a dated copy at every change, so a vintage accumulates from today.

jobs.name: state_claims_substate
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Unemployment claims below the state level, which the federal weekly file does not carry: Missouri by county every week since 2003, Connecticut initial and continued claims by week, New York by region monthly from 2003 and statewide from 1971 with beneficiaries, benefits paid and average duration, Michigan's own moving average. Never revised. Washington publishes claims by county and by industry every week but changes the file's number each time, so it is fetched by the dynamic_links job instead.

jobs.name: state_warn
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Layoff notices with the employer, the date and the number of workers, from the three states that publish them as data rather than as a web page: Texas daily and append-only, California's live workbook for the current fiscal year, Colorado's own sheet with permanent, temporary, furlough and reduced-hours counts separated. Real time by construction and never revised. The other states publish WARN as HTML or PDF only; the Cleveland Fed file in collection 199 remains the aggregator for those.

jobs.name: state_fiscal
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What states actually collect each month, which moves before any survey: New York's monthly tax collections with withholding tax separated (the fastest single fiscal series in the country), Texas general revenue and all funds monthly with sales-tax allocations by county and by city, Massachusetts transaction-level revenue. Monthly, never revised.

jobs.name: state_programs
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Counts of people on federal programmes by state, monthly: food assistance persons, households and benefits, and Medicaid and children's health applications and enrolment. The Medicaid file carries its own preliminary-or-updated flag, so vintages come with it. Both rise in a recession before any survey records it.

jobs.name: energy_hf
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The highest-frequency measure of activity that exists and is never revised: hourly electricity demand by balancing authority, six months to a file. With it the weekly petroleum and gas prices by state, weekly gas storage, and the keyless bulk archives for petroleum, gas and electricity by state.

jobs.name: regional_fed
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The regional banks' own surveys and state indexes, monthly, diffusion, never revised once published: Philadelphia's state leading indexes (the file the ledger had been missing), its state coincident indexes and state business-cycle dates, its manufacturing history back to May 1968 and its non-manufacturing history; New York's Empire State manufacturing and business leaders services surveys; the three Dallas surveys; Richmond manufacturing back to 1993; the Chicago Midwest index with its state contributions.

jobs.name: census_hf
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The Census business survey that asks firms every two weeks how the last two weeks went, by state and by sector. Biweekly, never revised, and the only official series in the country at that frequency with a state dimension.

jobs.name: bls_state_detail
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Job openings, hires, quits and layoffs by state, and the gross job gains and losses behind the net payroll number by state and county. The turnover file is the state-level form of the objects the rule's own proposers read.

jobs.name: freight_travel
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Movement by state, monthly and never revised: trucks, containers and people crossing the northern and southern borders by port and state; departures, passengers and freight by airport; the transportation services index. The border file is an unusually early state-level signal for Texas, Arizona, California, Michigan, New York and Washington.

jobs.name: housing_listings
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Listings as they stand, by state and by county, monthly with a weekly national file: active inventory, days on market, new listings, price cuts. Restated each vintage, which is why a dated copy is kept at every change.

jobs.name: vintage_databases
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The record of what each number was when it was first published, which is the thing the rule's causal standard is built on. The Philadelphia real-time set is the canonical American vintage database and covers series ALFRED does not; the five workbooks already held are joined here by industrial production, the consumer price index, housing starts and the first, second and third releases of payrolls. With them the OECD's revisions database, whose EDITION dimension is the vintage, the Canadian release log that timestamps every series to the minute, and the Cleveland Fed's own revised-versus-original inflation files.

jobs.name: nowcast_comparators
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What the published nowcasts said on each day, which is what the rule must be printed beside in Paper 2. The Atlanta workbook holds every vintage of its own forecast and its subcomponents; the Philadelphia daily index and the Cleveland daily inflation files change each day; the anxious index is a professional forecaster's own probability that output falls, quarterly since 1968, and is the closest published comparator to a recession call there is.

jobs.name: labour_postings
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Hiring as it happens: the daily index of job postings nationally and by state, the small-business jobs index and wage growth by state and metro from a payroll processor, and the running layoff tracker. Daily and monthly, never revised. The state postings file is a daily state panel, which nothing else in the warehouse provides.

jobs.name: stress_daily
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Daily measures of financial stress and funding that are published once and never revised: the Office of Financial Research's stress index back to 2000 with its five components, tri-party repo rates, the New York Fed's reference rates with their own revision flag, dealer positions, the System's holdings, bank failures and quarterly call reports, and short interest with its revision flag.

jobs.name: text_attention
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What was being said and looked up, daily and never revised: news sentiment back to 1980, daily policy uncertainty, equity market volatility attributed to news, geopolitical risk daily, trade policy uncertainty, and the System's own speeches and press releases as dated event feeds.

jobs.name: surveys_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Three survey files the warehouse did not hold in their raw form: the Michigan index back to 1952 as published, the New York Fed's consumer expectations microdata, and the global supply chain pressure index.

jobs.name: intl_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Keyless national services the collector had not been asking: the euro area's quarterly accounts, the Bank of England's daily database, the Bank for International Settlements' policy rates, Australia's labour force, the International Labour Organization's monthly unemployment for the United States on its own definition, the OECD's composite leading indicators, and every Treasury auction with its bid-to-cover.

jobs.name: state_business_formation
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Businesses being started and stopped, at the finest grain any government publishes. Census counts applications by state every week in a keyless file (the API now demands a key; this file does not). New York lists every corporate filing the day it is made, with the county; Colorado lists every entity with its formation date and every later transaction, so dissolutions can be counted as well as formations; Oregon, Connecticut and Delaware list registrations and licences; Texas and Pennsylvania list active permits, which is a count of establishments.

jobs.name: state_spending_receipts
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What people actually spend, collected by tax authorities rather than asked in a survey. Texas taxes every bar and restaurant's alcohol receipts and publishes them per establishment per month with the county, which is a discretionary-consumption series at sub-state grain. New York publishes lottery sales per retailer per day, which is the highest-frequency free spending proxy found anywhere in this search.

jobs.name: state_labour_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Claims cut by industry and by age in Missouri, and Colorado's own labour files, which are worth having for one reason beyond their content: the unemployment estimates carry preliminary and benchmark flags, so the state itself declares which numbers are not final. Colorado also publishes state-level job openings, hires, quits and layoffs back to December 2000.

jobs.name: state_distress
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Households losing their homes, which no labour series records. The Eviction Lab file is weekly at census-tract level for most states and is still being updated despite a file name that says 2021; Connecticut publishes the same by tract; Maryland publishes foreclosure notices by county monthly and eviction cases one by one; Texas publishes landlord and tenant caseload by county and precinct.

jobs.name: state_safety_net
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Food assistance by county in Pennsylvania, individuals and dollars, monthly back to 2004, which is finer than the federal file; and Connecticut's monthly counts by programme.

jobs.name: state_indexes_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Three state-level indexes the warehouse lacked: the Dallas Fed's Texas leading index, the New York Fed's household debt and delinquency by state, and economic policy uncertainty by state, monthly from 1985, which is the only state-level uncertainty measure that exists.

jobs.name: transit_activity
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Public transport ridership by agency with the state attached, monthly: people going to work, counted at the turnstile. Reached through the transportation department's Socrata portal, because its own host refuses a plain client.

jobs.name: bankruptcy_district
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The federal courts publish bankruptcy filings by district only once a quarter. Individual bankruptcy courts publish their own monthly counts; Oregon's is a plain table by chapter, month and division and is the most readable of them. A crawl of the other ninety-three districts is a later job.

jobs.name: lehd_quarterly_workforce
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The Quarterly Workforce Indicators as flat files, which need no key where the Census API now does: hires, separations, turnover, job creation and destruction, and earnings, by county and industry, quarterly. The twelve largest states first; the rest follow when the disk allows. Heavily revised each vintage, which is itself the reason to date every copy.

jobs.name: discover
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The collector's own search. api.us.socrata.com indexes every open-data portal in the United States, so one question reaches all of them; two national CKAN catalogues are asked the same questions after. A match must pass a relevance pattern, must not already be held, must have its own newest observation within three years (asked of the dataset itself, because a portal's updatedAt is metadata churn: Colorado's foreclosure files carry today's date and end in 2016), and must fit the pass's budget. Everything kept is listed in warehouse/discovered/discovered_registry.csv with the date column and the newest observation found.

jobs.name: derive_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Reduces the new sources to the two-column date-and-value form the rule and the quality gate read: weekly business applications, layoff notices and the workers named in them, daily lottery sales, monthly alcohol receipts, claims by county summed to the state, food assistance, transit trips, eviction filings, job postings, financial stress and policy uncertainty. Runs after the fetchers each cycle.

jobs.name: discovered_promoted
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The datasets the collector found for itself that were worth keeping, promoted out of the discovery folder into a job of their own so they are maintained with a dated copy at every change rather than fetched once. Washington's construction intents (every project notified to the state, 293 MB, current), Virginia taxable sales by locality for every year published, Connecticut's monthly tax revenue, refunds and alcohol tax, California disability insurance claims monthly, Colorado liquor licences approved and surrendered (a count of businesses opening and closing), Oregon spirits sales by city, and New York City job postings.

jobs.name: state_warn_all
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026 after the coverage map in collection 215 showed layoff notices held for three states of fifty-one. Every address here was fetched and its contents read before it was written down. Three states publish nothing at all - Arkansas cites its own statute, New Hampshire takes enquiries by electronic mail, Wyoming publishes only the rules - and Oklahoma's list renders only in a browser. Nebraska's endpoint still answers but the state stopped filling it after 2020, and North Dakota's cumulative file has not moved since October 2023; both are kept so that the day they resume is recorded. Richest by far is Illinois: 4,889 notices with thirty-four columns back to 1987.

jobs.name: state_revenue
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Monthly tax collections were held for five states. The Census Bureau's experimental workbook carries all fifty-one at once from April 2019 to March 2025 - discontinued, which is why the live feeds below matter - and the rest are each state's own monthly report. Withholding tax, the fastest labour signal in public finance, is broken out separately by Utah, Michigan, Maryland and Arizona. Illinois publishes daily. Nine states publish only through a browser-rendered dashboard and are left out rather than half-registered.

jobs.name: state_hours_earnings
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Average weekly hours and hourly and weekly earnings by state, which the national rule reads as factory hours and which the warehouse held only nationally. Manufacturing hours for all employees cover 46 states and for production workers all 52 state codes, monthly from 2007, not seasonally adjusted. The series identifier carries the state and the data type, so the whole panel is in these files: 02 hours, 03 hourly earnings, 11 weekly earnings, 07 and 08 the production-worker forms.

jobs.name: state_credit
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The state counterpart of the national rule's credit leg. Bank call reports summed by state give assets, loans, past-due and charge-offs; the consumer bureau publishes the share of mortgages thirty and ninety days late by state, monthly from 2008; the Small Business Administration publishes every approved loan with the borrower's state and the approval date, which is a monthly count of credit actually extended to small firms. The mortgage and loan files are restated with each vintage, which is why a dated copy is kept at every change.

jobs.name: state_activity_hf
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The fastest state-level measures that exist free, all published once and not revised: petrol prices for every state daily, coal production by state weekly, the weekly price series the Energy Information Administration keeps for nine states, industrial gas deliveries by state, and Oklahoma's daily files of drilling permits and completions. Federal contract obligations by state are asked of the spending service directly.

jobs.name: state_search_trends
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What each state is searching for, today. The feed is a snapshot with no history endpoint anywhere, so this series exists only from the day we begin keeping it - which is the argument for keeping it now rather than when it is wanted. A dated copy is kept at every change, so the archive builds itself.

jobs.name: state_surveys
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The only free state-level purchasing managers' survey in the country: Creighton's nine-state Mid-America index, with new orders, production, delivery lead time, inventories and employment for each of Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, Oklahoma and South Dakota, published on the first business day of the month and never revised; with it the ten-state rural bank survey, and the Atlanta Fed's firm cost expectations for its district.

jobs.name: dated_backfill
jobs._note: Split out of dated_files on 18 Sep 2026. Walking four hundred dated addresses for the permit and revenue histories had taken the hourly cycle from twenty seconds to eleven minutes. The deep backfills run on the six-hour thread; the current months stay hourly. Both mark an address that answers 404, so a month not yet published costs one request.

jobs.name: state_check
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Runs the state coverage map and the state validator every six hours, so that a hole or an impossible value in the state panel is found by the machine rather than by a paper.

jobs.name: state_grid_load
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Electricity actually drawn, below the state line, within hours. Texas publishes load for each of eight weather zones and New York for each of eleven load zones; both are meter readings and are never revised. The Texas index is a list of documents, so the collector keeps the index and the downloader follows it; New York's file is one a day at a dated address.

jobs.name: state_housing_weekly
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Six weekly housing files, eight hundred metropolitan areas each carrying its state name, to the week ending about thirteen days ago: new listings, for-sale inventory, new pending sales, median list price, days to pending, and the share of listings whose price was cut. The state-level versions of these files do not exist; the metro files aggregate to states by their own state column. The whole history is restated at each release, which is why a dated copy is kept every time one changes.

jobs.name: state_health_weekly
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Weekly and daily measures by state that arrive within six days, which is faster than any labour series and which a recession moves through hours worked, insurance and deferred care. The Delphi service is kept beside them because it publishes an issue date with every observation, so it can be read as it stood on a past day - the only file in this group that can.

jobs.name: state_daily_activity
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Daily counts with a place attached: journeys and toll crossings in New York two days behind, building permits issued in New York City, Chicago and Austin within a day or two, and boardings in Chicago. Permits issued daily are the only construction signal below the month that exists free.

jobs.name: state_warn_pages
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Six more state layoff-notice lists that exist only as pages. A dated copy is kept every time the page changes, so the notices accumulate with the date they appeared even though the state publishes no file.

jobs.name: grid_all_states
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026 as the all-states backbone for electricity, replacing three single-operator feeds as the object. Sixty balancing authorities in one file and every sub-region in another: the thirteen-state eastern market by twenty-one zones, the midcontinent by six, New England by eight, the southwest power pool by seventeen, New York by eleven, California by four, Texas by eight, New Mexico by nine, the Dakotas and Wyoming by three, and the southeast and northwest by authority. Hourly, one to two hours behind. The raw demand column is never revised; the adjusted one is. Alaska and Hawaii have no balancing authority and therefore no hourly load anywhere - that is the whole of the gap, and it is the country's, not ours.

jobs.name: state_energy_production
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Production and electricity sales by state, monthly, for every producing state at once, so that the two states whose regulators publish daily files stop being the object. Crude oil, natural gas withdrawals, and retail electricity sales and revenue by state and sector. Mine employment and production by state quarterly from the mine safety administration.

jobs.name: state_fuel_prices
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The daily page covering all fifty-one is already held; this adds the official weekly workbook, which carries the nine states that have their own series plus every refining district, so that each of the other forty-two states has an official regional series to be checked against. New York publishes its own eleven regions weekly.

jobs.name: state_retail_sales
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Lottery sales exist as data in two states only, so they cannot be the object. Retail sales as reported to state revenue departments are the substitute and exist in far more states; Colorado's file, by county and industry and month, is the template, and the same object is sought in every other state by the discovery job. Casino and sports-wagering revenue in Connecticut joins them as the same family of discretionary spending.

jobs.name: state_housing_backbone
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. State-level housing where the weekly files are metropolitan: the state home-value index and the state market tracker, both carrying all fifty-one.

jobs.name: permits_daily_metro
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026, and marked an EXTRA rather than an object. Permits issued daily in twenty places. The state permit object remains the Census monthly file, which covers all fifty-one; these are detail on top of it and must never be read as a state series, because the twenty-nine states without such a feed would silently read as zero.

jobs.name: warn_token_sites
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Georgia's layoff notices are served only to a request carrying a token the page mints on each load. The page is read and the tokens tried in turn until one is accepted, every cycle. This was the last state whose notices were reachable at all without a browser.

jobs.name: state_social_programs
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. People turning to the state when work fails, by state and month. Disability claims are the centre of it: the workload file carries applications, pending cases, determinations and allowance rates for every state monthly from October 2000, and applications rise when work is scarce. With them the supplemental income recipients and payments by state, and the assistance caseloads. The Social Security host answers only to a complete browser identity, which the fetch engine supplies through its curl rung.

jobs.name: state_federal_employment
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Federal civilian employment by duty station, quarterly, with the hires and separations behind it. Federal employment moves against the cycle in some states and with policy in others, and it is a fifth of the payroll in several. The archives refuse a request that does not name the page they are linked from.

jobs.name: state_banking_credit
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Where deposits sit and where credit is extended, by state. Branch-level deposits with the county attached; every credit union's call report; and every mortgage application in the country with its state, outcome and amount, which is the finest picture of household credit that exists free.

jobs.name: state_census_bulk
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The Census bulk files, which need no key where its interface now demands one. Firm entry and exit by state, which is the cleanest measure of business death there is; establishments and employment by state and county; poverty and median income; population; state tax collections quarterly and annually; and building permits by county every month.

jobs.name: state_households
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. How households are faring, by state: rents, vacancy and how long a home sits on the market monthly; homelessness counts and shelter beds annually; fair market rents by county; where people moved between states; income by postcode; and college enrolment, which rises when work is scarce.

jobs.name: state_activity_extra
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Four more state series with real cyclical content and short lags: firearm background checks monthly by state, which the literature treats as a prompt proxy for household activity and which arrives within a fortnight; motor-vehicle registrations by state; farm income by state; and the weekly crop report, which is a state-by-state field survey published the next day.

jobs.name: state_weekly_conditions
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026, and the most valuable state object found in any sweep. The Boston Fed's weekly index of economic conditions covers all fifty states with a six-day lag and runs back to April 1987, which means a state-level test can be run weekly over four decades rather than monthly over two. The normalised file is kept beside the raw one. With it the daily index of job postings by state: the address used earlier pointed at the wrong repository and never answered, which is why postings had been missing from the state panel.

jobs.name: state_retail_and_spending
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Monthly retail sales by state and by trade category, the state counterpart of the national retail report, with its standard errors and its coverage file; and consumer complaints by state, which arrive within days and rise when households are under strain.

jobs.name: state_carrier_activity
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Trucking turns before almost anything else, and the federal motor carrier administration publishes its register daily: which operating authorities were granted and which revoked, which carriers were put out of service, and the carrier file that attaches a state to each docket. Together they are daily business formation and failure in the industry that moves first. Never revised; the record is the record.

jobs.name: state_federal_flows
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Money the federal government puts into each state, and the loans it guarantees there. Contract obligations by place of performance for any window; small-business lending by project state, monthly and only two and a half weeks behind, which is the promptest credit series with a state dimension found anywhere; flood claims and policies by state; marketplace enrolment; and student-loan balances and borrower counts by state.

jobs.name: state_firm_formation
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Who is starting businesses in each state and who is being licensed to trade. The entrepreneurship indicators by state, and the alcohol permits issued since the last publication, which is a licence count for an industry that opens and closes with the cycle. With them the household debt and delinquency figures by state and the college enrolment appendix, which rises when work is scarce.

jobs.name: industry_census_bulk
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. The Census bulk endpoint, which serves a whole programme as one file and asks for no key where the interface now demands one. Manufacturers' shipments, inventories and orders across eighty-seven categories, with new orders and unfilled orders separated - unfilled orders being the clearest forward-looking series in the manufacturing data. The advance durables file two weeks earlier. The quarterly services survey down to six-digit industry. The quarterly financial report, which is profits, sales and balance sheets by manufacturing industry. Construction spending by type, including the manufacturing category that has moved so much lately. And the inventory-to-sales ratios.

jobs.name: state_by_industry
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026, and the scarcest thing in the warehouse: measures that are state AND industry at once. The workforce indicators give quarterly flows by state and six-digit industry - firm job gains, firm job losses, hires, separations, turnover, earnings - which is what a rule about job destruction actually wants. The employment and wages census gives one file per area and one per industry, quarterly, to six digits. The establishment census gives counts and payroll by state, county and six-digit industry. Firm size detail says whether small firms or large ones are shedding. Non-employer businesses count the self-employed, who vanish from payroll measures entirely.

jobs.name: industry_prices_productivity
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. What industries charge and what it costs them to produce. Producer prices by industry to six-digit detail and by commodity back to 1967; import and export prices across sixteen hundred series; and productivity and unit labour cost by industry. Prices turn before volumes in several industries, and unit labour cost is the margin squeeze that precedes a layoff.

jobs.name: industry_capacity
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Capacity utilisation for thirty-nine industries as a flat file, and the whole production release as one package: two and a half thousand series, including a hundred and seventy-one utilisation series and the twelve motor-vehicle assembly series, which are a weekly-to-monthly physical count of cars and trucks actually built and which fall early and hard.

jobs.name: industry_company_filings
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Every quarter the Securities and Exchange Commission publishes the numeric facts of every filing, with the filer's industry code and its state of business address. That is company-level revenue, income and balance sheet by industry and by state, at a grain no statistical agency produces, about a month after the quarter closes. The rule cannot read it directly, but a measure of how many firms in an industry and a state reported falling revenue is buildable from it and from nothing else free.

jobs.name: industry_high_frequency
jobs._note: Added 18 Sep 2026. Industry activity faster than a month. The rail file reports carloads in twenty-two commodity categories and grain cars loaded BY STATE, weekly and two days behind, which is the only weekly state-and-industry physical measure found anywhere. Job postings by sector daily. And the keyless series endpoint for the industrial production and orders series that have no flat file of their own.
